evals.name: figma-url-ast-dashboard-review
evals.prompt: Review this Figma dashboard from the perspective of the air-surveillance-tech persona: https://figma.com/design/ops/Air-Picture-Validation?node-id=1-2. I need feedback on whether the screen supports track validation, weather discrimination, and sensor-health coordination during a normal watch. Please prioritize operational risks over generic UX comments.
evals.expected_output: Maps the request to air-surveillance-tech, loads only that persona, uses the Figma URL path, scopes the review to the provided dashboard, and produces a persona-grounded critique focused on track validation, weather discrimination, sensor-health coordination, cognitive load, system visibility, and operationally prioritized recommendations rather than generic UX advice.
assertions: Identifies or clearly uses the air-surveillance-tech persona rather than a generic operator persona.
Treats the Figma URL as the primary design input and acknowledges the dashboard/screen review scope.
Connects findings to documented AST responsibilities, systems, communications, or pain points such as track validation, RS-4, ERSA, BCS-F, sensor health, or juggling multiple systems.
Prioritizes operational impact and workflow fit instead of generic visual-polish advice.
Includes actionable recommendations tied to the persona context.

evals.name: loose-role-mapping-weapons-director
evals.prompt: Can you do a persona review of this fighter-control workflow for the weapons director role? The Figma frame is here: https://figma.com/design/ops/Fighter-Intercept?node-id=22-14. I'm less interested in colors and more interested in whether it supports comms, intercept decision-making, and not overloading the operator when things get busy.
evals.expected_output: Maps the loose role phrase 'weapons director' to the correct weapons-director persona, reviews the workflow from that role's communication and tactical-decision perspective, deprioritizes generic styling comments, and highlights high-tempo workflow, communications, and overload risks with actionable recommendations.
assertions: Maps the loose role wording to the weapons-director persona without requiring an unnecessary clarification when the match is unambiguous.
Frames the critique around fighter-control communications, intercept/tactical actions, or high-tempo workload rather than generic UX commentary.
Avoids focusing on colors or style-guide feedback as the primary output.
Provides role-specific, actionable recommendations grounded in responsibilities or pain points.

evals.name: screenshot-fallback-mcc
evals.prompt: I can't use Figma MCP right now, but I need a persona-based review for the mission-crew-commander of a mission summary screen. Assume I can only share screenshots. Please review for decision support, crew coordination, and whether the layout matches the tempo of a busy mission commander. Be explicit about any limits caused by the screenshot-only input.
evals.expected_output: Uses the mission-crew-commander persona, proceeds with a screenshot-only fallback path, explicitly states scope limits caused by missing MCP/design-state access, and still delivers an actionable persona-grounded review centered on decision support, crew coordination, and mission tempo.
assertions: Uses a screenshot-only fallback approach rather than assuming live Figma access.
Explicitly states evidence limits or uncertainty caused by screenshot-only review.
Keeps the review grounded in the mission-crew-commander role instead of generic stakeholder feedback.
Provides actionable recommendations despite limited design access.

evals.name: outline-unavailable-ast
evals.prompt: Please review a surveillance screen for air-surveillance-tech. Figma access is available, but Outline docs are not. I want to know whether the design reduces context switching across BCS-F, RS-4, and ERSA and whether it helps with the valid/not-valid decision. Call out what extra documentation would have made the review stronger.
evals.expected_output: Performs the AST review without blocking on Outline, clearly notes that supporting-doc evidence is unavailable, evaluates context switching and valid/not-valid decision support using the persona profile, and mentions which missing standards or source materials would strengthen the review.
assertions: Does not block the review on Outline access being unavailable.
Explicitly notes the lack of supporting documentation and names useful missing context such as standards, prior reviews, specs, or training material.
Connects the critique to AST systems and decision workflow, especially BCS-F, RS-4, ERSA, or valid/not-valid decisions.
Maintains persona-grounded operational analysis despite missing docs.

evals.name: ambiguous-persona-clarification
evals.prompt: Can you review this air-defense console from the director perspective? I want persona-based feedback on whether it helps with tactical calls and coordination, but I'm not sure whether I mean the weapons role or the senior one.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that 'director' is ambiguous, lists the closest available persona options, asks the user to choose rather than guessing, and avoids producing a full review until the persona ambiguity is resolved.
assertions: Recognizes the persona request is ambiguous rather than assuming a specific director persona.
Lists or references the closest available persona options, such as weapons-director and senior-director.
Asks the user to choose the intended persona before continuing with the full review.
Avoids pretending the ambiguity is resolved when it is not.

evals.name: invalid-persona-request
evals.prompt: Do a persona review of this radar settings panel for the intel analyst persona. If that persona doesn't exist, tell me what operator personas are available so I can pick the right one.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent an intel-analyst persona, states that the requested persona is unavailable, and offers the available personas from the index so the user can choose a supported role.
assertions: Does not fabricate a missing persona.
States that the requested intel-analyst persona is unavailable or unsupported.
Offers available personas or directs the user to choose from the supported list.
Defers the actual review until a valid persona is selected.

evals.name: comparison-request-should-not-load-multiple-by-default
evals.prompt: I want a persona review of this control panel for surveillance-tech. Keep it focused on that role only. Do not compare it against any other personas unless I ask. The main question is whether the panel supports continuity of detection and doesn't bury the first actions the operator needs to take.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the review scoped to the surveillance-tech persona only, does not broaden into unnecessary multi-persona comparison, and critiques the panel in terms of detection continuity, first actions, and role-specific workflow support.
assertions: Keeps the review scoped to the requested surveillance-tech persona only.
Does not introduce multi-persona comparison unless explicitly requested.
Focuses findings on surveillance-tech workflow concerns such as detection continuity or first actions.
Provides actionable, role-specific recommendations.

evals.name: evidence-and-uncertainty-discipline
evals.prompt: Review this Figma flow for the senior-director persona and be careful not to overstate anything. We only have a partial workflow and a few annotations. I want the review to distinguish observed evidence from inference, especially around approval authority and mission-planning decisions.
evals.expected_output: Uses the senior-director persona, reviews the partial flow with explicit scope limits, separates observed evidence from reasonable inference, and avoids overstating conclusions about approval authority or mission-planning behavior while still providing useful recommendations.
assertions: Acknowledges the design evidence is partial.
Separates observed evidence from inference or uncertainty in the review.
Keeps the analysis grounded in the senior-director role and approval/mission-planning context.
Avoids overconfident claims while still offering practical recommendations.

evals.name: generic-ux-near-miss-negative
evals.prompt: Can you give this Figma file a quick UX pass and tell me if the spacing, button styles, and typography feel polished? No need to tie it to a role or workflow; I just want generic UI feedback.
evals.expected_output: Should not force a persona-based review workflow onto a request that explicitly asks for generic UI feedback without a role or workflow. A strong response would either decline to use persona framing, note that persona review is not the right fit as stated, or ask whether the user wants a role-specific review instead.
assertions: Recognizes this is a generic UI review request, not a strong fit for persona-based critique as written.
Does not invent a persona or produce a full persona-grounded review without role context.
Either redirects toward generic UX feedback or asks whether the user wants a persona-specific review instead.

evals.name: non-figma-operator-guidance-near-miss-negative
evals.prompt: I need help writing a training SOP for new surveillance operators. This isn't a design review — it's more about documenting the steps they should follow on shift.
evals.expected_output: Should not treat the request as a persona-based Figma/UX review. A strong response would recognize the task is SOP writing rather than interface critique and avoid forcing the persona-review workflow.
assertions: Recognizes the request is for SOP/process writing rather than design review.
Does not force a persona-review critique structure onto the task.
If it responds helpfully, it redirects toward documentation or writing support instead of pretending this skill is the right fit.
